name: Breakpoint Container
description: Perspective Breakpoint Container - responsive container that switches between completely different layouts based on session width
author: GitWay

defaultView.description: Default view to display (small, medium, or large)

smallBreakpoint.description: Minimum width in pixels for small breakpoint (typically 0px)

mediumBreakpoint.description: Minimum width in pixels for medium breakpoint (typically 768px for tablets)

largeBreakpoint.description: Minimum width in pixels for large breakpoint (typically 1024px for desktops)

smallViewPath.description: Path to view for small breakpoint (mobile devices)

smallViewParams.description: Parameters to pass to small breakpoint view

mediumViewPath.description: Path to view for medium breakpoint (tablets)

mediumViewParams.description: Parameters to pass to medium breakpoint view

largeViewPath.description: Path to view for large breakpoint (desktops)

largeViewParams.description: Parameters to pass to large breakpoint view

transitionDuration.description: Duration of transition animation when switching breakpoints

enableTransitions.description: Enable transition animations when switching between breakpoints

position.description: CSS position property for container (inherited by child components)

notes: Ideal for completely different layouts between mobile and desktop
Components in each breakpoint are completely separate instances
Unlike Flex containers, provides discrete breakpoint switching
Position property is inherited by child components
Breakpoints based on session width, not device width
Useful when Flex container doesn't provide desired responsiveness

small.commonUse: Single column layouts, simplified navigation, touch-optimized controls

medium.commonUse: Two column layouts, collapsible sidebars, adaptive navigation

large.commonUse: Multi-column layouts, full navigation, expanded controls

responsiveDesignPatterns: Mobile-first: Design small breakpoint first, enhance for larger screens
Desktop-first: Design large breakpoint first, simplify for smaller screens
Component-based: Each breakpoint uses different component sets
Layout-based: Same components, different arrangements per breakpoint

viewInheritance.position: Inherited by components in breakpoint container
viewInheritance.fixed: Components fixed to viewport (rare use case)

performanceConsiderations: Each breakpoint loads separate view instance
Only active breakpoint view is rendered
State not preserved when switching breakpoints
Consider view load time for breakpoint transitions

comparisonToFlexContainer.breakpointContainer: Completely different views per breakpoint, discrete switching, separate component trees
comparisonToFlexContainer.flexContainer: Same components with responsive flex layouts, continuous resizing, shared component tree

commonUseCases: Header that switches from icon to full logo
Different dashboard layouts for phones vs tablets vs desktops
Simplified mobile UIs with full-featured desktop versions
Touch-optimized mobile controls vs mouse-optimized desktop controls
Different data visualization approaches per device type

parameterPassing.separate: Each breakpoint can receive different parameters
parameterPassing.shared: Pass same data with different presentation
parameterPassing.consistency: Maintain parameter structure across breakpoints for easier development

designBestPractices: Maintain consistent functionality across all breakpoints
Test at exact breakpoint widths (767px, 1023px) for edge cases
Use meaningful content hierarchy appropriate to screen size
Provide clear visual feedback during breakpoint transitions
Avoid hiding critical features on smaller breakpoints
scriptingCapabilities: Access current active breakpoint via scripting
Detect breakpoint changes with event handlers

dashboard.small: Single column, stacked widgets, simplified charts
dashboard.medium: Two columns, resizable widgets, standard charts
dashboard.large: Three columns, drag-drop widgets, advanced charts
